children: Steel prices have surged to four-year high of ₹63,800 a tonne after an increase ₹1,600 a tonne week-on-week (w-on-w) ended September 18, on the back of restocking by the trade and distributors amid fear of further rally in prices.
Rebar prices rose ₹2,300 a tonne w-on-w to ₹60,450 a tonne, marking a renewed uptrend after seasonal moderation in June quarter.
BigMint benchmark Mumbai HRC assessment rose by ₹1,200 a tonne to ₹63,900 a tonne while CRC prices jumped ₹1,300 a tonne to ₹73,500 a tonne.
Major producers increased HRC prices by about ₹750-1,750 a tonne and CRC prices by ₹1,500-2,000 a tonne, prompting corresponding increased across trade markets, it said.

Post-monsoon revival of infrastructure projects also supported domestic demand and prices. On the cost front, imported coking coal prices moved up 22 per cent to $283 a tonne against an average of $232 a tonne in August due to growing supply concerns.
NMDC increased 65.5 per cent FE content iron ore prices by ₹150 per tonne to ₹5,400 per tonne but retained the lower grade 64 per cent fines at ₹4,500 a tonne.
Geopolitical tensions continue to exert pressure on raw-material, freight and supply-chain volatility. The steel supply in the domestic markets also remained tight.

India’s crude steel production edged down 0.1 per cent year-on-year to 14.1 million tonne in August, while finished steel consumption rose 4 per cent y-on-y to 14.32 mt. Finished steel imports rose 8 per cent y-on-y to 0.72 mt, while exports increased 31 per cent to 0.69 mt.

Bhavik Bhagwanji Shah, Analyst (Metals & Mining), Choice Institutional Equities said post-monsoon demand from infrastructure, construction and automotive sectors, together with higher coking-coal costs, could provide further support to domestic steel prices.
However, he added the ability of mills to pass through further increases will depend on import flows and downstream demand.
The rise in steel prices will impact MSMEs, particularly in the downstream sectors such as auto components, engineering, fasteners, fabrication and construction-linked segments, he said.

The immediate impact is likely to be margin pressure and higher working-capital requirements, as smaller manufacturers generally have less pricing power than integrated steelmakers and large OEMs, he added.

Vandana Bharti, Head of Commodity Research, SMC Global Securities said driven by geopolitical tensions, global and regional steel markets face selective upward pressure primarily from escalating energy, power generation and maritime freight overheads, establishing a structural cost floor beneath raw materials such as imported ferrous scrap.

Instead of triggering runaway price spikes, these cost-push factors are counter-balanced by subdued real estate demand in key consumer markets such as China, leaving broader markets relatively range-bound, she said.

title: Steel prices hit 4-yr high on rise in cost amid strong demand
